docs.cap.backlog.body: Per-project backlog read from the Tradvia store.
docs.cap.backlog.title: Backlog
docs.cap.cards.body: Every card is a durable state machine (card-state.v1.json contract). The dashboard shows the board from the store. Durable waiting and resume (#40) is Planned.
docs.cap.cards.title: Cards
docs.cap.connections.body: The "Connections" screen (admin role): provider and model per flow role (planner/executor/reviewer/orchestrator), and each AI provider's secret (an API key, or the Claude Code subscription token). Today only the orchestrator role (the chat) actually uses the choice; the other roles still only read the configuration, without applying it. The chat works only with an AI provider configured with an API key (Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini); without one it is off and the panel says why. The Claude Code subscription token runs the executor only, never the chat. An API key is the only method for Anthropic/Gemini/OpenAI — none of the three currently offers a browser login for third-party apps the way the Claude Code subscription does (see ADR 0019).
docs.cap.connections.title: Connections
docs.cap.create.body: Create, start, order and answer cards in the dashboard. Available now.
docs.cap.create.title: Create cards in Tradvia
docs.cap.deploys.body: Approve or reject pending production deploys, cancel replaced ones and run the post-deploy operation, with an audit entry. Same status as PRs: needs the GitHub App permissions.
docs.cap.deploys.title: Deploys
docs.cap.kpis.body: Success rate, median duration, merged PRs and cost per card, read from the store. See dashboard-kpis.md. Costs are estimates, not an invoice.
docs.cap.kpis.title: KPIs
docs.cap.plans.body: @Agent-Architect posts the plan on the issue and asks for approval in chat (Discord). Approving, rejecting or asking for changes resumes the run.
docs.cap.plans.title: Plans
docs.cap.prs.body: The card shows the PR, its checks and the per-file diff; a maintainer can squash-merge with their own GitHub token. Tested offline; production needs the GitHub App permissions.
docs.cap.prs.title: Pull requests
docs.cap.signin.body: Sign in with GitHub, sessions and per-project roles. Available now.
docs.cap.signin.title: Sign-in
docs.guideTitle: How to run a task in Tradvia
docs.statusNote: Real status, mirroring ADR 0007 and the README. Only Shipped means available; In progress, Partial and Planned are never described as available.
docs.step.create.body: Create the card in the Tradvia dashboard. You can also start from a GitHub issue: mention @claude or apply the labels described in hello-world.md.
docs.step.create.title: Create the card
docs.step.deploy.body: Pending production deploys appear in the dashboard to approve or reject. Same conditions as the previous step.
docs.step.deploy.title: Approve the deploy
docs.step.plan.body: @Agent-Architect asks in Discord. Reply “Aprovado”, “Rejeitado” or describe the change; the run resumes where it stopped. Approval in the dashboard does not exist yet.
docs.step.plan.title: Approve the plan
docs.step.pr.body: On the card, see the executor summary, files and the core-tests, license-boundary and cla checks; then squash-merge. Requires GitHub sign-in and the GitHub App permissions; until then, merge on GitHub.
docs.step.pr.title: Review and merge the PR
docs.step.run.body: Open the dashboard: card board, recent activity, runs and KPIs, read from the store and refreshed automatically.
docs.step.run.title: Follow the run
docs.tech.endpointsNote: The endpoints exist in the code; that does not make the capability Shipped (see the statuses above).
docs.tech.intro: core/ (FSL-1.1-ALv2) never imports from ee/ (commercial license); make boundary checks it. The API lives under /api/* (core/src/tradvia/api.py) and this static dashboard under /runs/. Card state follows card-state.v1.json. Per-project interactions are configured in .tradvia.yml (example).
docs.tech.manualNote: every guide and ADR, with contents and search, read here in Tradvia
docs.title: Documentation
docs.trouble.1.body: Use the panel published at app.tradvia.org. In a local copy or at another address, the panel reads GitHub without signing in, and GitHub allows only 60 requests per hour for your IP. If “GitHub API rate limit reached” appears, wait up to an hour or open app.tradvia.org.
docs.trouble.1.title: Check the address
docs.trouble.2.body: If you are signed in, click Sign out at the top of the page, sign in again with GitHub and reload. An old session can leave the screen without data.
docs.trouble.2.title: Sign out and back in
docs.trouble.3.body: If the address ends in #settings or #help, that screen shows instead of the panel. The filters in the URL (from, to, executor, fcard, status) narrow the cards: open the address without them to see everything.
docs.trouble.3.title: Check the page address
docs.trouble.4.body: Failures appear in the status bar, above the board. If there is no message, open the browser console (F12, Console tab) and note the first red error.
docs.trouble.4.title: Read the error message
docs.trouble.5.body: Press Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on Mac) to load the latest version of the page.
docs.trouble.5.title: Reload without cache
docs.trouble.footer: If a feature described on this page is missing from the panel, the published version is older: the panel is updated only after the change is merged into main and the production deploy is approved.
